root_cause: A branching process instance (base step -> DMN gateway -> extra-approve) risked writing a PHANTOM `instance.ended` transition-journal event on approve#1 (the intermediate step), before the engine actually ended the instance. That phantom completion would distort the process_transition_journal / cycle-time analytics (src/db/transition-journal.ts: loadInstanceJournal / loadCycleTimeByActivity count instance.ended). Investigation found the behavioural guard ALREADY present on the base (dev@8e291098): `instance.ended` is emitted from EXACTLY ONE call site — reconcileInstanceEngineDrive -> appendInstanceEnded in src/http/process-projection.ts — inside `if (endedResult.ended)`, reached only when engine.isInstanceEnded() confirms. appendTaskApproved stopped emitting it in T-0443 (commit f453ff31); the single engine-gated emit gate was introduced by T-0522 (commit 71292644). The remaining gap was that this analytics-protecting invariant was pinned only by fake-pool unit tests (src/__tests__/inbox-engine-drive.test.ts 8b/8c), never against real Postgres/JSONB + the transition-journal reader.
fix: No behavioural change was required — the correct engine-gated guard already exists. This task (changes_product=0, substrate/analytics) delivers the missing real-Postgres regression test that pins the invariant, plus a documenting comment at the guard so a future refactor cannot silently drop it. Emit call-site guarded: src/http/process-projection.ts, reconcileInstanceEngineDrive step 2 — `if (endedResult.ended) { ... appendInstanceEnded(...) }`. Guard condition: emit `instance.ended` ONLY when engine.isInstanceEnded(instanceId) reports ended:true; the 'not really ended' signal (a live post-gateway process.next_task / !isInstanceEnded) falls through to step 3 which surfaces the next step instead of ending.

The LINEAR regression test still passed under the mutation (it genuinely ends). GREEN: restoring `if (endedResult.ended)` -> both tests pass (2/2). Verified src diff carries no behavioural change (only the documenting comment).
